lines.text: Ugh... my head. Wait... where is everything? Where did the whole world go?
No houses. No roads. No tools. I don't even have a knife.
It's just me... and a wild valley I've never seen before.
Okay. I'm Zero. If the world got reset, then today is day one. And I'm rebuilding it, from zero.
So... what do I do first? Because if I pick wrong out here, it could actually kill me.
Find food? Build a house? Make fire? I need all of them. But none of them comes first.
If I don't know what's around me, every choice I make is just a guess.
So step one: learn the land. What's useful out there, and what's dangerous.
Here's the plan. Before sunset, I learn this valley, and I pick one safe spot for my first base.
The catch? I've only got half a day. I'm already thirsty. And I have nothing. Literally nothing.
Let's start right here. Grass under my feet. And the soil... firm. Not soggy at all.
So water doesn't sit here for long. That's a good sign for a place to live.
But wow, this sun. In heat like this you sweat fast, and you can dry out before you even notice.
Working hard on a really hot day, a person can sweat out more than a liter an hour.
So I watch for the warning signs. Thirst, a headache, dark pee. And I've already got the thirst.
Water is urgent, I know. But first, I need to know which way is which.
This stick will do. Nice and straight. It's not a tool yet, but it can show me direction.
Push it in, standing straight up... and a pebble right at the tip of its shadow.
Now I wait. The sun crosses the sky from east to west, so the shadow slowly swings the other way.
Second pebble, at the new tip. First pebble to second... that line runs roughly west to east.
And if I know west and east, I know north and south too. I've got a compass, made by the sun!
The problem is, from down here he can't see far. Tall grass and trees block almost every direction.
To understand the whole valley, he has to look from somewhere high.
Zero walks to a huge boulder to the north, and carefully climbs up, one step at a time.
And from up here, the whole valley opens up.
Before he explores further, let's look at the rule survival experts use to set priorities. It's called the rule of threes.
A person can last about three minutes without air, and about three hours in harsh weather without shelter.
About three days without water, and about three weeks without food.
But in heat, with hard work, the body runs out of water much faster than that.
These numbers are only rough estimates, not hard rules. But they make it very clear what's most urgent.
Zero already has air. So next come shelter and water. Food can wait.
And both shelter and water start with the same question: where?
Good shelter is close enough to walk to water, but not so close the water can flood it. And near the materials you'll build with.
A good way to explore is to split the land into directions, and ask every direction the same three questions.
What here is useful? What here can hurt me? And if something goes wrong, which way do I run?
That last one is the one people forget. But it matters most, because when danger really comes, there's no time to think.
To the north, the valley opens into plains, with a river winding all the way to distant mountains.
But Zero spots a huge dark cloud to the right. Rain here could come fast, and heavy.
To the west: thick jungle. Wood, vines, and big leaves. A great source of materials.
But in the jungle you can't see far, it's easy to get lost, and there may be animals you can't see.
To the east: a wide river. Water, stones, and gravel.
But a river also has currents, and a water level that can change with the rain.
And to the south, a long, tall cliff stands like a wall, with a green hill in front of it.
Cliffs give shade and stone. But rocks can also fall from above.
Now Zero has the big picture. The next step is to go down and check each place for real.
Zero memorizes the view, and plans a route. West first, then east, then around to the south, before the hottest part of the day.
First stop: the jungle edge in the west. Vines hang everywhere. He gives one a pull. Really strong.
Vines like these could be used for tying things later. Zero remembers this spot.
There's a bush full of bright red berries. They look delicious. But Zero stops his hand.
Unknown fruit can be poisonous. The simple rule: if you're not one hundred percent sure, don't eat it.
Deeper in the jungle, light barely reaches the ground. Every direction looks the same.
Zero snaps small branches so they hang down, every so often. Markers to find his way back.
Without markers, on the way back every tree looks the same. People get lost in forests even when the way out isn't far at all.
Second stop: the river in the east. The water is slow, shallow, and so clear you can see the pebbles on the bottom.
Zero is really thirsty, but he doesn't drink yet. Clear water looks safe. But that still needs to be proven.
Further upstream, the water gets faster and stronger, until it turns into white rapids.
The water is so loud you can barely hear anything else. The rocks at the edge are wet, and covered in slippery algae.
Fast water only knee deep can already knock a person over. This is no place to go in. Ever.
Along the other bank, the ground is clay. Step on it, and you slip, and sink to your ankles.
But clay like this could be very useful one day. So Zero marks it in his mind, too.
Third stop: the foot of the southern cliff. The rocks here come in many colors. Some are deep red.
Zero doesn't know what these red rocks are yet. But a color that's different from the rocks around it often means some mineral is mixed in.
The broken rock piled up at the bottom of the cliff tells him rocks fall from up there, again and again.
So Zero doesn't stand under the cliff for long, and notices how far the big rocks have rolled. That's the danger zone.
Walking along the cliff, Zero finds a rock shelter, an overhang sticking out like a roof.
A natural place to hide from rain. But first, he has to check if an animal already lives here.
There are animal tracks, and fur stuck on the rocks. This place already has an owner. Zero quietly backs away.
It's late afternoon. Zero needs to choose a place for his base. And he finds one that looks perfect.
A sandbar at the river bend. Flat ground, soft, close to water, and full of driftwood to use.
It looks like the best place for a base in the whole valley.
He lies there listening to the gentle water, and thinks: tonight, I'm sleeping right here.
Until he looks up, and sees dry grass and sticks caught in a bush, higher than his own head.
This is a flood line. When the river floods, it leaves debris at the highest point the water reached.
Which means the whole sandbar he's standing on has been underwater before.
And the driftwood that looked like a gift is proof the water carried it here from somewhere else.
Dead leaves caught in the reeds line up at the same height too. Every sign points to the same answer.
If he built his base here, one night of heavy rain could wash everything away. Including him.
Lesson one: the place that looks the most convenient can be the most dangerous.
Zero heads back to the meadow, near the big tree he saw this morning.
The ground here is several meters higher than the river. No flood lines. And the soil is dry.
But before deciding, he looks up and checks the branches above.
There's a big dead branch hanging up there. Branches like that can break and fall at any moment, especially in strong wind.
So Zero moves out from under that branch. He still gets afternoon shade, but he's not under the risk.
Just a few steps can be the difference between safe and hurt.
Time for the same three questions. Is anything useful nearby? Wood from the jungle is less than five minutes away, and the river isn't far.
Is there danger? He's above the flood line, away from falling rocks, and out from under the dead branch.
If something goes wrong, which way does he run? From here he can see all around, and run out in any direction.
Finally, Zero uses a stick to draw a map in the dirt. The river, the jungle, the cliff, and every danger he found today.
Then he plants the stick right here. This is the very first base of the new world.
From now on, every time he has to make a decision, Zero has this map: what's where, and what to avoid.
So, today's lesson. Before you build anything, know the land. Look from high ground, split it into directions, and ask three questions everywhere.
And remember: the place that looks most convenient is the place you should check most carefully.
Unlocked: a survey map, and the first base site.
But all day, Zero hasn't had a single drop of water. And the river looks so clear and tempting.
Is water that clear really safe to drink? Next time, we find out.
